messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a quick, step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and safely: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give it a light clean (wipe down the fretboard, strings, body) and tune it to standard pitch (E‑A‑D‑G‑B‑E). | A well‑tuned, clean instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take Quality Photos** | Shoot from multiple angles (headstock, neck, body, back, bridge, electronics if any). Use natural light, avoid glare. | Good photos attract buyers and reduce questions. | | **3. Write a Clear Description** | Include brand, model, year, serial number, condition (“excellent”), any upgrades (new strings, pickups), and why you’re selling. | Transparency builds trust and speeds up negotiations. | | **4. Set a Competitive Price** | Research similar listings on eBay, Reverb, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local classifieds. Aim slightly above your target to leave room for negotiation. | Pricing right the first time reduces back‑and‑forth and attracts serious offers. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform(s)** | • **Online Marketplaces** – eBay, Reverb, Etsy (for vintage gear)
• **Local Classifieds** – Craigslist, Gumtree, Nextdoor
• **Social Media** – Facebook Marketplace, Instagram Stories/Posts, dedicated guitar groups
• **Music Stores** – Many retailers buy used gear or offer consignment services | Using multiple venues maximizes exposure; local platforms cut shipping hassles. | | **6. Draft a Safe Transaction Plan** | • For local sales: meet in a public place (coffee shop, police station parking lot).
• For shipping: use a sturdy padded case, insure the package, and ship via tracked service (UPS, FedEx, USPS Priority Mail).
• For online escrow: consider PayPal Goods & Services or Reverb’s payment protection. | Safety and tracking protect both parties and reduce disputes. | | **7. Negotiate & Finalize** | Be prepared to negotiate but know your lowest acceptable price. Once agreed, confirm details (pickup location, payment method, shipping label). | Clear communication prevents misunderstandings. | | **8. Ship or Hand‑Over** | If shipping, pack securely, label clearly, and drop off at the carrier. If local, hand over the instrument and collect payment immediately. | Proper packaging and prompt payment ensure a smooth transaction. | ### Quick Tips - **Serial Number**: Keep it handy—buyers often ask for it to verify authenticity. - **Condition Notes**: Mention any scratches, fret wear, or repairs. Honesty reduces returns. - **Return Policy**: Offer a short return window (e.g., 48 hrs) for buyer peace of mind, especially if shipping. - **Safety First**: Never accept cash from strangers in private homes; prefer secure payment methods. --- #### Example Listing Template ``` Title: 2010 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition – $350 Description: - Brand/Model: Yamaha FG800 - Year: 2010 - Serial #: 12345678 - Condition: Excellent (no visible damage, new strings) - Features: Solid spruce top, rosewood back & sides, 25.5" scale - Reason for sale: Upgrading to a larger instrument Price: $350 (Negotiable) Photos: [Attach 5–6 high‑resolution images] Contact: DM me on Facebook or email me at example@email.com ``` Feel free to adapt this template to fit your guitar’s specifics. Good luck with your sale!
